newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE men to sail to Iraq with food, medicine.
newsitem.headline: UAE men to sail to Iraq with food, medicine.

text.p: Ten men from the United Arab Emirates will set sail for Iraq on Tuesday to deliver 32 tonnes of milk and medicine to help ease the suffering of Iraqi children under U.N. sanctions.
It would be the first such visit since Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait strained Iraq's ties with the UAE, organisers said.
The trip to the southern Iraqi port of Umm Qasr follows a November appeal by UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan for reconciliation with Iraq.
"We are not looking at any (political) factors as our eyes are focused only on the suffering of Iraqi children," Mohammad bin Abdullah bin Shabib, one of the organisers, told Reuters.
He said the organisers were a group of friends, mostly bankers and businessmen.

"We hear all the time and read in the newspapers that Iraqi children are dying every day because of lack of food and medicine," bin Shabib said. "Hence we decided to embark on the 'first friendship trip' and to organise more trips in the future after we gather facts on the situation of children in Iraq from hospitals and officials during this visit."
The United Nations Children's Fund UNICEF said in November that 4,500 children were dying each month in Iraq from hunger and disease.

Sheikh Mohammad bin Rashid al-Maktoum, crown prince of the UAE emirate of Dubai and the UAE's defence minister, donated humanitarian supplies worth 1.5 million dirhams ($410,000) to the initiative, bin Shabib said.
He said his group was also banking on pledges of support from local food merchants and the start of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan next week to raise future donations.
Iraq says U.N. trade sanctions imposed after its invasion of Kuwait have deprived it of cash to buy food and medical supplies that are exempted from the embargo.
Iraqis relying on food rations for more than six years will have to wait a little longer before seeing the fruits of a newly implemented oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
